I'm planning a new project called "Arche" — a tech-stack-agnostic boilerplate/framework for AI-powered (Claude Code) software engineering. It will generalize the AI-governance patterns found in this repo (zimmermann-pwa) into a reusable foundation that any project can build on top of, regardless of language/framework.

I need you to explore and report on the SKILLS and SCRIPTS surface of this repo so I can decide what generalizes vs. what is Zimmermann/Salesforce-specific.

Explore thoroughly:
1. `.claude/skills/` — every subdirectory. For each skill, read its SKILL.md and note: (a) its name and purpose, (b) whether its logic is generic to any project or hard-coded to Zimmermann/Salesforce/PWA specifics, (c) any supporting files/scripts it references. Pay special attention to: session-start, onboarding, project-init, scope-check, audit-tier, code-quality, feature-spec, pr-checklist, new-component, qa-generate, generate-changelog, upstream-sync-review.
2. `scripts/` — every script (e.g. switchEnv.mjs, syncCursorRules.mjs, hooks/pre-commit, hooks/commit-msg, contentful/, any state-detection script used by project-init). For each, note what it does and whether the mechanism is generic or tied to this stack.
3. Note how skills reference `.claude/rules/` and `.docs/` so I understand the cross-references.

Report back a structured inventory: for each skill and script, a one-line purpose and a GENERIC / ZIMMERMANN-SPECIFIC / HYBRID classification with a short reason. Do not dump full file contents — summarize. Call out anything that looks like a reusable "AI operating system" primitive (governance, memory, workflow, enforcement).

1	# Skills — What They Are and How to Use Them
2	
3	This is the canonical reference for every skill in this folder. If you're looking for _why_
4	the skill system exists (the human-in-the-lead design philosophy), see the
5	[Human-in-the-Lead AI Development — Project Setup Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305102849)
6	Confluence page (Part 2: AI Governance Layer) —
7	that page covers the rationale; this file covers the _mechanics_: what each skill does, what
8	to pass it, and what it hands back.
9	
10	## How skills work
11	
12	- Invoke a skill by typing `/skill-name` (optionally followed by an argument) in a Claude
13	  Code session. Each skill is a structured, reviewable process defined in its own
14	  `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` file — not a freeform prompt.
15	- Where a skill takes an argument, its `SKILL.md` uses `$ARGUMENTS` to capture whatever
16	  follows the skill name, e.g. `/new-component productBadge` or `/audit-tier overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.ts`.
17	  If you invoke a skill with no argument and one is expected, Claude asks for it.
18	- Every skill is **human-in-the-lead**: it either stops for confirmation at a defined
19	  checkpoint, or produces a read-only report/plan rather than making changes outright.
20	  See the checkpoint column in each table below.
21	- These `SKILL.md` files are also the master source for `.cursor/rules/skills/*.mdc` and
22	  `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md` — see [scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs](../../scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs).
23	  Edit the `SKILL.md` here, then run `npm run sync:ai-rules:fix`; never edit the generated
24	  Cursor/VS Code files directly.

Run on a **first session on a new machine or first day on the project**.                    | Confirms understanding at each phase before moving on             |

Use before editing anything you're unsure about.                                                                                                                                          | Tells you who to notify before you touch the file                        |

Use after props change, or to audit everything at once. | Report only — you resolve any drift found                                                                 |

68	## Release management
69	
70	| Skill                                                    | Usage                                                                                    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                                                    |
71	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
72	| [`/generate-changelog`](generate-changelog/SKILL.md)     | `/generate-changelog` (then answers version/range questions)                             | Builds a structured, four-audience changelog (dev team, QA, product, GitHub Release) from conventional commits and the upstream baseline. Use before cutting a release branch.                                      | You review the changelog before it's published; the GitHub Release command is proposed, never run automatically |

75	## Adding a new skill
76	
77	1. Create `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter (see any existing skill for the format).

1	---
2	name: session-start
3	description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
4	---
5	
6	Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.
7	
8	## Steps (in order — do not skip any)
9	
10	1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.
11	
12	2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
13	   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
14	   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
15	   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
16	   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
17	   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.
18	
19	3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
20	   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.
21	
22	4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
23	   - Current branch
24	   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
25	   - The last completed task and the next task
26	   - Any blockers or outstanding issues
27	
28	   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."
29	
30	5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.
31	
32	Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Living Memory — what belongs where
37	
38	`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.
39	
40	**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.
41	
42	| File | What belongs there | When to update |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
45	| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
46	| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
47	| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
48	| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |
49	
50	**Rules:**
51	- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
52	- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
53	- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

1	---
2	name: onboarding
3	description: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
4	---
5	
6	Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.
7	Then proceed through the phases below. Ask one question at a time. Do not front-load.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Role and context
12	
13	Ask:
14	> "Are you joining as a developer or a QA engineer?"
15	
16	Wait for the answer. Then:
17	
18	**If developer:** Ask:
19	> "Which squad are you on — Squad A (checkout, cart, payments, order management, tax, GivX) or Squad B (Homepage, PDP, PLP, search, account, Brochureware Content)?"
20	
21	**If QA:** No squad question needed — QA covers both squads.
22	
23	Ask (both roles):
24	> "Is this your first time working on this project, or are you returning on a new machine?"
25	
26	New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks
31	
32	Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.
33	
34	```bash
35	node --version
36	npm --version
37	claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
38	git branch --show-current
39	ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
40	[ -f .env.shared ] || echo ".env.shared missing"
41	for t in dev test sit uat staging prod; do
42	  [ -f ".env.$t" ] || echo ".env.$t missing"
43	done
44	[ -f .env ] || echo ".env missing"
45	```
46	
47	For each issue found:
48	
49	**Hooks missing:**
50	> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
51	```bash
52	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
53	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
54	```
55	Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`
56	
57	**On develop or main:**
58	> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
59	```bash
60	git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
61	```
62	
63	**Not fully initialized yet** (`.env.shared` missing, or any `.env.<tier>` file missing):
64	> "Environment config isn't fully set up on this machine yet. Run:"
65	```bash
66	npm run env -- init
67	```
68	> "This scaffolds `.env.shared` (values shared across every tier) and one `.env.<tier>` file per
69	> deployment tier (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), pulls in whatever's already been published to
70	> this repo's GitHub Environments (Settings > Environments), and auto-fetches your Contentful
71	> Delivery/Preview tokens once you've filled in a personal `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`.
72	> Fill in any values it reports as still blank — `npm run env -- validate` shows what's missing —
73	> then activate a tier with `npm run env -- dev` (or whichever tier you're working against).
74	> Full command reference is in `.env.sample`'s header comment."
75	> `init` skips any file that already exists and only scaffolds what's missing, so it's always
76	> safe to rerun on a partially-initialized machine.
77	
78	**Fully initialized but no tier activated yet** (`.env.shared` and every `.env.<tier>` file present, but root `.env` missing):
79	> "Environment config is initialized but no tier is active yet. Activate one:"
80	```bash
81	npm run env -- dev
82	```
83	> "(or whichever tier you're working against)."
84	
85	**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.
86	
87	**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.
88	
89	Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Phase 3 — Developer orientation
94	
95	*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*
96	
97	### Rules overview
98	
99	Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.
100	
101	**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
102	> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
103	> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."
104	
105	**Protection tiers:**
106	> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
107	> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
108	> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."
109	
110	Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).
111	
112	**TypeScript-only rule:**
113	> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
114	> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
115	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."
116	
117	**Hard Rule #12:**
118	> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
119	> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."
120	
121	**Contact map:**
122	Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
123	> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
124	> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."
125	
126	### Sprint order
127	
128	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Tell them which sprint the project is currently in.
129	
130	> "We're in Sprint [N]. That means [what exists]. Code from Sprint [N+1] doesn't exist yet —
131	> don't reference it in your tasks."
132	
133	### Squad-specific orientation
134	
135	**Squad A (checkout, cart, payments):**
136	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/order-summary/`,
137	> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
138	> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."
139	
140	**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
141	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
142	> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
143	> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."
144	
145	### Key skills
146	
147	Tell them which skills to reach for first:
148	- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
149	- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
150	- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
151	- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
152	- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey
153	
154	### First task
155	
156	> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.
157	> Then run `/session-start` to see the current project state.
158	> When you have a ticket to work on, start with `/feature-spec` before writing any code."
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Phase 4 — QA orientation
163	
164	*Skip this phase for developers — they went through Phase 3.*
165	
166	### The QA model
167	
168	> "This project uses a human-in-the-lead QA model. Claude generates tests — you validate them.
169	> A test is not complete until you have approved the Gherkin `.feature` file.
170	> Never accept a Playwright spec without reading and confirming the `.feature` file first."
171	
172	### Testing layers
173	
174	Three layers, three purposes (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing):
175	1. **Vitest** — unit logic.
176	2. **Storybook `play` functions** — component interactions.
177	3. **Playwright** — E2E user journeys (this is where Gherkin lives).
178	
179	### Feature file workflow
180	
181	Walk through the workflow:
182	1. Developer creates a Jira story.
183	2. Developer runs [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) in Claude Code.
184	3. Claude drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops**.
185	4. QA reads the `.feature` file — it's in `e2e/features/{area}/`.
186	5. QA annotates corrections in the file with `# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]`.
187	6. Developer runs `/qa-generate` again with the annotation.
188	7. Claude updates the feature file (confirm), then generates the Playwright spec.
189

34	   - Split cross-squad work into two separate prompts

2	name: audit-tier
3	description: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
4	---
5	
6	Identify the protection tier and owner of a file or directory in this codebase.
7	
8	The path to audit is: $ARGUMENTS
9	
10	## What to output
11	
12	**1. Tier**
13	- Tier 1 (Frozen) — must not be modified without explicit owner approval
14	- Tier 2 (Protected) — feature branch only, requires second-developer PR review
15	- Tier 3 (Squad-owned) — only the owning squad should be prompting Claude here
16	- Tier 4 (Feature-local) — freely editable on a feature branch
17	
18	Check against:
19	- [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) for Tier 1
20	- [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md) for Tier 2
21	- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` for Tier 3 *(if absent, infer from path: checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B)*
22	
23	**2. Owner**
24	Design System / Integration / SI Partner / Squad A / Squad B / Both Squads
25	
26	**3. Can Claude Code modify it?**
27	- Tier 1: No. Developer must name the file explicitly in the prompt AND confirm owner approval.
28	- Tier 2: Yes on a feature branch — second-developer PR review required before merging.
29	- Tier 3: Yes — but only the owning squad should be running Claude in this area.
30	- Tier 4: Yes, freely.
31	
32	**4. Import blast radius**
33	Run this to check how many non-test, non-story files import it (from `overrides/app/` — the customisation surface):
34	```bash
35	grep -rl "$(basename "$ARGUMENTS" | sed 's/\.[tj]sx\?$//')" overrides/app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" \
36	  | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v '\.stories\.' | wc -l
37	```
38	If more than 5, flag it as **high blast radius** — a change here breaks many consumers.
39	
40	**5. Next step**
41	Specific action for the developer — e.g.:
42	- "Message #design-system before asking Claude to touch this"
43	- "This is Tier 3 Squad A — if you're Squad B, message the Squad A Lead first"
44	- "This is Tier 4 — safe to include in your prompt with an explicit file path"

1	---
2	name: code-quality
3	description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
4	---
5	
6	Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
7	diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Input
12	
13	The user will provide one of:
14	- A file path or directory to audit
15	- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`
16	
17	If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
18	Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Parallel execution
23	
24	For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
25	as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
26	bundle all checks into one agent.
27	
28	- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
29	- **Agent B — Import analysis**
30	- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
31	- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**
32	
33	For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Agent A — Naming & structure
38	
39	Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
40	(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
41	[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
42	ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
43	that's how the files drift apart.
44	
45	Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:
46	
47	- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
48	- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
49	- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
50	  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
51	  structure**.
52	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
53	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.
54	
55	For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
56	anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Agent B — Import analysis
61	
62	For each file, read the import statements and check:
63	
64	- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
65	  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
66	- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
67	  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
68	  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
69	- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
70	- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Agent C — TypeScript coverage
75	
76	Check each file against the relevant rule file:
77	
78	- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
79	  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
80	  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
81	- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
82	  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
83	- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
84	  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).
85	
86	Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
87	errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Agent D — Test & story coverage
92	
93	For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
94	- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
95	- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
96	- If a test file exists, verify:
97	  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
98	  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
99	  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
100	- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
101	- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.
102	
103	For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
104	- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
105	  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
106	  one-liners are exempt.
107	- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
108	  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).
109	
110	---
111	
112	## Output format
113	
114	Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:
115	
116	```
117	## Code Quality Report
118	**Scope:** [files audited]
119	**Branch:** [current branch]
120	**Date:** [today]
121	
122	### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
123	[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]
124	
125	### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
126	[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]
127	
128	### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
129	[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]
130	
131	### ✅ No issues found
132	[List checks that passed cleanly]
133	
134	### Summary
135	X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
136	```
137	
138	Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
139	Do not modify any files — report only.
140

1	---
2	name: feature-spec
3	description: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
4	---
5	
6	Produce a scoped implementation spec for a feature before any code is written.
7	Follow each phase in order. Do not write code — this skill produces a plan only.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Clarification (one question at a time)
12	
13	Read the feature description the user has provided.
14	
15	Identify what is unclear or under-specified. Then ask ONE clarifying question — the most
16	important one. Wait for the answer. Ask the next question only after receiving a response.
17	
18	Continue until you have answers to all of these (stop earlier if the feature is simple):
19	
20	- Which sprint does this belong to? (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present)
21	- Which PRD in [.docs/prd/](../../../.docs/prd/) is the source of truth for this feature? Cite section + requirement ID.
22	- Is this Zimmermann-specific or an enhancement to an existing PWA Kit pattern?
23	- Which squad owns the primary files involved? (A: checkout/cart/payments — B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
24	- Are there any Tier 1 or Tier 2 files that will need to change?
25	- Does this touch any third-party integration (Global-e, Adyen, Contentful, Searchspring/Einstein, Didomi, Omneo, Emarsys, AP21, Narvar, Google Maps)?
26	- What does "done" look like — what is the acceptance criterion?
27	- Are there any consent / Didomi gating requirements for scripts the feature loads?
28	
29	Do not ask about things the feature description already makes clear.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
34	
35	Once clarification is complete, spawn three agents in parallel to research the codebase.
36	Each agent is independent and self-contained.
37	
38	**Agent A — Registry / file scan:**
39	_If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read `.claude/registry/components.md`,
40	`hooks.md`, and `utils.md`. _Otherwise_, do a direct scan: `find overrides/app/components overrides/app/hooks overrides/app/utils -type f` and grep for anything relevant.
41	Return: a list of relevant existing assets with their file paths.
42	
43	**Agent B — Pattern scan:**
44	Find the most similar existing feature in the codebase under `overrides/app/`.
45	Look for a component or page that has a similar interaction pattern or data shape.
46	Read its implementation to understand the conventions used (how it calls hooks, how it
47	handles loading/error states, how it structures its JSX, which Chakra components it uses).
48	Return: the path of the most similar existing implementation and a brief description of
49	the pattern it uses.
50	
51	**Agent C — Upstream check:**
52	Search `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for any existing upstream implementation
53	of this feature or a related one. If found, assess whether the copy-first override workflow
54	(see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) — "Copy-first rule") should be applied.
55	Return: upstream file path if found, and a Take / Override / Skip recommendation.
56	
57	Wait for all three agents to return before proceeding to Phase 3.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Phase 3 — Sprint check
62	
63	Reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (when present) and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md).
64	
65	State which sprint this feature belongs to and confirm all its dependencies exist.
66	If the feature requires something from a later sprint, say so explicitly:
67	
68	> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work and does not exist yet."
69	
70	Ask the developer whether to proceed with a placeholder or wait.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Phase 4 — Spec output
75	
76	Produce the implementation spec in this format:
77	
78	---
79	
80	```markdown
81	## Feature Spec: [Feature Name]
82	
83	**PRD source:** [.docs/prd/<file>.md § <section> — <REQ-ID>]
84	**Sprint:** [N]
85	**Squad:** [A / B / Both]
86	**Estimated scope:** [S / M / L — S = 1 file, M = 2-5 files, L = 6+ files]
87	
88	### New files to create
89	
90	| File path         | What it is                               |
91	| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
92	| overrides/app/... | [component / hook / util / test / story] |
93	
94	### Existing files to modify
95	
96	| File path | Tier      | Change needed |
97	| --------- | --------- | ------------- |
98	| [path]    | [1/2/3/4] | [description] |
99	
100	### Copy-first overrides required
101	
102	| Base file (node_modules) | Target path under overrides/ | TS conversion needed? |
103	| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------- |
104	
105	### Hooks involved

2	name: qa-generate
3	description: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
4	---
5	
6	QA test generation is a two-step, human-gated process. Do not generate the Playwright spec
7	until the `.feature` file has been explicitly confirmed by Lead QA.
8	
9	> **Three testing layers in this project** (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md)):
10	> - Vitest — unit logic
11	> - Storybook `play` functions — component interactions
12	> - Playwright — E2E user journeys (this skill)
13	>
14	> The gherkin → Playwright workflow below is the **E2E layer only**. It does not replace
15	> the Vitest / Storybook layers — write all three where each applies.
16	
17	> **Status:** the `e2e/` directory and Playwright harness must be in place before running this skill.
18	> If `e2e/` does not yet exist, stop and tell the developer the QA harness must land first.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Phase 1 — Gather story details
23	
24	Ask these questions one at a time. Wait for the answer before asking the next.
25	
26	1. What is the Jira story key? (e.g. SFCC-142)
27	2. What is the story title?
28	3. What are the acceptance criteria? (paste them directly)
29	4. Which squad owns this story? (Squad A: checkout/cart/payments — Squad B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
30	5. Which sprint is this? (Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — flag if the story references a later-sprint dependency)
31	6. Is this a P0 journey? (P0 = Digital SIT gate critical path: guest checkout, registered checkout, PDP variant selection, ATC, auth)
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Phase 2 — Draft the .feature file
36	
37	Write the Gherkin file to:
38	`e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature`
39	
40	Follow the standard in `e2e/features/README.md`:
41	- Tags: `@{JIRA-KEY} @{area}` — add `@p0` if confirmed in Phase 1
42	- Feature block with persona, goal, and value
43	- Background block for shared preconditions
44	- At least one happy path scenario and one failure/edge scenario
45	- Plain English only — no selectors, URLs, or implementation detail
46	- Under 150 lines — split by scenario group if longer
47	
48	**Stop here. Do not generate the Playwright test yet.**
49	
50	Present the draft and say:
51	> "This is the draft `.feature` file. Please share it with Lead QA for validation.
52	> When QA has approved or annotated it, reply with their feedback and I will proceed."
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Phase 3 — Apply QA annotations (if any)
57	
58	If Lead QA returns annotations in this format:
59	```
60	# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]
61	```
62	
63	Update the `.feature` file to reflect the correction. Confirm the change explicitly:
64	> "Updated [what changed]. No other changes made."
65	
66	Repeat until Lead QA confirms the file is correct.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Phase 4 — Generate the Playwright spec
71	
72	Only proceed when Lead QA has confirmed the `.feature` file.
73	
74	Write the Playwright test to:
75	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts` — for standard tests
76	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.p0.spec.ts` — for P0 tests
77	
78	Rules:
79	- Files are TypeScript (`.spec.ts`) — the TS-only convention applies to E2E too.
80	- Import Page Objects from `e2e/support/pages/` — never use raw selectors in the test file.
81	- Selector priority in POMs: accessible selectors (role + accessible name, label, text) > semantic HTML attributes (alt, title) > `data-testid` (only when no semantics apply). See [.claude/rules/testing.md](../../rules/testing.md).
82	- Import fixtures from `e2e/fixtures/` — never hardcode test data. Fixtures must be keyed by `SITE_ID` (Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 11 active locales).
83	- Test description must match the Scenario name in the `.feature` file exactly.
84	- Use `waitForSelector` or `waitForResponse` — never `waitForTimeout`.
85	- Under 200 lines — extract shared logic to `e2e/support/helpers/` if needed.
86	- **Every `test()` call must carry two Playwright tags: the `.feature` file's `@area` tag AND
87	  its `@{JIRA-KEY}` tag** from Phase 2, e.g. `test('...', {tag: ['@checkout', '@SFCC-142']},
88	  async ({page}) => {...})`. The `@area` tag is what `develop`-targeted PRs use to run only the
89	  specs relevant to a diff — see [.claude/rules/testing.md > Change-scoped
90	  E2E](../../rules/testing.md#change-scoped-e2e-develop-targeted-prs-only). The `@{JIRA-KEY}`
91	  tag is what lets `e2e-browserstack` scope a Zephyr-linked BrowserStack run to just this
92	  story when its key is referenced on a PR — see [.claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story
93	  scoping](../../rules/testing.md#browserstack-story-scoping). A missing or mismatched `@area`
94	  tag doesn't lose coverage (the full-suite fallback still catches it) but a missing
95	  `@{JIRA-KEY}` tag means BrowserStack has nothing to run for this story at all — get both right.
96	- **If `{area}` doesn't already have an allow-list group in `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s
97	  `detect-changes` job** (check the `Get changed files` step — `e2e_checkout` exists today),
98	  flag this to the developer: a new area needs its own allow-list group added there before
99	  scoping will work for it. Propose the group (the paths this spec's Page Objects and the
100	  component/page folders it exercises live under) rather than adding it yourself, since it's a
101	  Tier 1 CI/CD file — see [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md).
102	
103	---
104	
105	## Phase 5 — Check for new Page Object needs
106	
107	Read the generated test. If it references an element not yet in any Page Object:
108	- Propose the addition to the relevant `e2e/support/pages/*.ts` file.
109	- Do not create a new Page Object file without confirming the path first.
110	- Page Object files stay under 150 lines — propose a split if exceeded.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Phase 6 — Summary
115	
116	List every file created or modified:
117	- `.feature` file path
118	- `.spec.ts` file path
119	- Any Page Object additions
120	
121	Then say:
122	> "The `.feature` file requires Lead QA sign-off before this test is considered complete.
123	> If QA annotates further changes, run `/qa-generate` again with the updated story key."
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Notes
128	
129	- Never generate tests on `develop` or `main` — check `git branch --show-current` first.
130	- If the story references a component or hook from a later sprint (per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`),
131	  stop and flag it: the test may need to be deferred or the spec written with a placeholder.
132	- For Magento baseline regression tests, write to `e2e/features/regression/BASELINE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`
133	  and note that these files use a `@baseline @regression` tag set, not a Jira key tag.
134

3	description: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
4	---
5	
6	Generate a structured release changelog. Ask clarifying questions one at a time,
7	then research in parallel, then produce the output. Do not write code.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Establish the release range
12	
13	Ask these questions one at a time if not already provided:
14	
15	1. What is the release version? (e.g. `v1.2.0`)
16	2. What is the base ref to compare from? (default: run `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to find the last tag. If no tags exist yet, use the first commit.)
17	3. Is there anything specific that should be highlighted or excluded from the changelog?
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
22	
23	Spawn three agents simultaneously. Each is self-contained.
24	
25	**Agent A — Git log analysis**
26	Run: `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s" --no-merges`
27	Parse each commit by conventional type:
28	- `feat` → Features
29	- `fix` → Bug fixes
30	- `perf` → Performance
31	- `refactor` → Refactors (include in technical changelog only)
32	- `test` → Test coverage (include in technical changelog only)
33	- `docs` → Documentation (include in technical changelog only)
34	- `build` / `ci` → Infrastructure (include in technical changelog only)
35	- `chore` → Maintenance (omit from product/QA changelogs unless `chore(deps)`)
36	- `upstream-sync` → Upstream sync (separate section)
37	- `style` → Omit from all changelogs
38	
39	For each `feat` and `fix`, extract the scope (if present) and description.
40	Group commits under their type. Return the full categorised list.
41	
42	**Agent B — Upstream baseline scan**
43	Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
44	Identify whether the `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version changed between BASE_REF and HEAD.
45	Use `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md package.json` to find any bump.
46	Return: the version bump (if any) and a one-sentence summary.
47	
48	**Agent C — New components / hooks scan**
49	If `.claude/registry/` exists, run:
50	`git diff [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .claude/registry/`
51	and parse for new entries in `components.md`, `hooks.md`, `utils.md`, `pages.md`.
52	Otherwise, fall back to:
53	`git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --diff-filter=A --name-only -- 'overrides/app/components/**' 'overrides/app/hooks/**' 'overrides/app/pages/**' 'overrides/app/utils/**'`
54	Return: lists of new components, hooks, utils, and pages added in this release.
55	
56	Wait for all three agents before proceeding.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Phase 3 — Sprint context
61	
62	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Identify which sprint(s) were completed or progressed
63	in this release cycle. State it in one sentence for the product changelog.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Phase 4 — Generate the changelog
68	
69	Produce the following four sections. Write them into a single file at:
70	`docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md` (create the directory if it doesn't exist).
71	
72	---
73	
74	```markdown
75	# Release [VERSION] — [TODAY]
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 🛠 Technical Changelog (Dev Team)
80	
81	### New components & hooks
82	[From Agent C — list each new component and hook with its path under overrides/app/]
83	
84	### Features
85	[From Agent A feat commits — scope: description]
86	
87	### Bug fixes
88	[From Agent A fix commits — scope: description]
89	
90	### Performance
91	[From Agent A perf commits]
92	
93	### Upstream sync
94	[From Agent B — `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version bump (if any), what was reviewed]
95	
96	### Refactors & test coverage
97	[From Agent A refactor and test commits]
98	
99	### Dependencies & infrastructure
100	[From Agent A build, ci, chore(deps) commits]
101	
102	---
103	
104	## 🧪 QA Changelog (Test Team)
105	
106	### What changed that needs testing
107	[For each feat and fix commit, one bullet: what changed and which user journey to test.
108	Reference the relevant P0 test if one covers it. Flag any area where a P0 test does NOT exist.]
109	
110	### High-risk areas this release
111	[Any changes to: checkout flow, auth, pricing, cart, product display, navigation, consent (Didomi), international (Global-e).
112	State what specifically changed and the blast radius.]
113	
114	### Regression watch
115	[Any changes to shared components (Tier 2) or shared hooks. List the component and
116	all known consumers that should be spot-checked.]
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 📣 Product Changelog (Business / Stakeholders)
121	
122	### Sprint progress
123	[From Phase 3 — one sentence on sprint completion]
124	
125	### What's new
126	[feat commits only, in plain English, no technical detail. Group by user-facing feature area.]
127	
128	### What's fixed
129	[fix commits only, in plain English. Focus on customer-facing fixes only.]
130	
131	### What's coming next
132	[One sentence on the next sprint focus from .docs/memory/sprintScope.md]
133	
134	---
135	
136	## 🚀 GitHub Release Summary
137	
138	**[VERSION]** — [TODAY]
139	
140	[2–3 sentence summary suitable for the GitHub Release page. Highlights the biggest
141	feature additions and most significant fixes. Suitable for external visibility.]
142	
143	**Full changelog:** `docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md`
144	**Release notes reviewed by:** [FILL IN]
145	```
146	
147	---
148	
149	## Phase 5 — Offer GitHub Release draft
150	
151	After writing the file, ask:
152	> "Would you like me to create a GitHub Release draft using this summary?
153	> Run: `gh release create [VERSION] --draft --title '[VERSION]' --notes '[SUMMARY]'`"
154	
155	Do not run the command — provide it for the developer to execute.
156	
157	---
158

161	- If commits mix conventional and non-conventional format (transition period), flag
162	  the non-conventional commits separately as "Uncategorised" and note they couldn't

2	name: new-component
3	description: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
4	---
5	
6	Scaffold a new Zimmermann custom component.
7	
8	The component name is: $ARGUMENTS
9	
10	## Conventions
11	
12	Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) (naming, folder layout,
13	cross-cutting rules), [components.md](../../rules/components.md) (props types, JSDoc policy,
14	composition, Storybook categorisation), and [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra token usage)
15	— together the single source of truth for scaffolding. Higher-level project rules live in
16	[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do not restate rules here — read those files before
17	scaffolding.
18	
19	Key implications for scaffolding:
20	- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
21	  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).
22	- Props type named `<ComponentName>Props`, declared at the top of `index.tsx` by default.
23	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.
24	
25	## Steps
26	
27	1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.
28	
29	2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:
30	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
31	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
32	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
33	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
34	   - No data-fetching hooks of any kind (commerce SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or React Query) — accept data as props; the parent (a page or container component) owns data fetching. See components.md → Composition → Container/presentational separation.
35	
36	3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
37	   if a story is needed at all. Per [components.md](../../rules/components.md) →
38	   **Storybook**, purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
39	   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
40	   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
41	   - Pick the right category prefix from components.md — `Foundation/`, `Elements/`,
42	     `Layout/`, `Commerce/`, `Forms/`, `Pages/`, or `Contentful/`. Ask the developer if it's
43	     not obvious which one fits (with your recommendation).
44	   - `title: '<Category>/<ComponentName>'` (e.g. `'Commerce/ProductTile'`,
45	     `'Layout/Header'`).
46	   - At least one named export `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states only —
47	     not every prop combination.
48	   - Add a `play` function only if the component has interactive behaviour worth asserting.
49	
50	4. Optional: if the component owns non-trivial logic, also create `index.test.ts` (Vitest) in the same folder. Skip otherwise.
51	
52	5. Optional: if the props type exceeds ~30 lines or will be consumed by sibling files, move it to `types.ts` in the same folder. Otherwise leave it inline.
53	
54	6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero new errors.
55	
56	## Constraints
57	
58	- Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry).
59	- Do not add npm packages — see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7.
60	- Do not import from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` source directly — re-export from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths.
61	- For new icons, use `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`; if a needed icon is missing, ask the developer.
62	
63	## Output
64	
65	Tell the developer:
66	- The paths of every file created.
67	- The import to copy: `import <ComponentName> from '.../components/<componentName>'` (no filename — resolves via `index.tsx`).
68	- A one-sentence note on where it likely wires in, or ask if unsure.
69	- A reminder that `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passed.

2	name: upstream-sync-review
3	description: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
4	---
5	
6	This is a **slim overrides project** on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` — not a framework fork.
7	The policy is **"read the changelog, bump opportunistically"** — see [.docs/upstreamPolicy.md](../../../.docs/upstreamPolicy.md).
8	
9	This skill helps you review a candidate version bump before doing it.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Input
14	
15	Ask the developer:
16	> "What candidate `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version are we considering? Paste a link to the GitHub release notes or the version number."
17	
18	If they give just a version (e.g. `10.1.0`), generate the release notes URL:
19	`https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/tag/v<X.Y.Z>`
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Step 1 — Capture current state
24	
25	Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Note:
26	- Current version
27	- Reviewed-up-to version
28	- Any deferred items
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Step 2 — Read the release notes
33	
34	Fetch the GitHub release notes for the candidate version (and any intermediate versions
35	between current and candidate). Summarise:
36	- Security fixes
37	- SCAPI / SDK breaking changes
38	- New configuration options
39	- Bug fixes that affect surfaces we override
40	
41	The bump policy says: bump opportunistically only when a release contains **security** or
42	**SDK** changes that affect us. Otherwise stay put.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Step 3 — Map changes to our override surface
47	
48	For each notable change in the release notes, check whether we override the affected file
49	under `overrides/app/`. If yes, the upgrade may need a re-port of the override.
50

1	---
2	name: contentful-register-component
3	description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
4	allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Bash
5	---
6	
7	# Contentful Component Registration
8	
9	Studio Experiences definitions are now **generated from code** — you never write a
10	`defineComponents` entry by hand. The source of truth is the component's `Props` type,
11	annotated with `@cf` JSDoc tags.
12	
13	## Steps
14	
15	### 1. Move the component into `experiences/`
16	
17	The codegen only processes files under
18	`overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`. If the component isn't there yet,
19	move it (or create it) in that folder.
20	
21	### 2. Add `/** @cf-register */` to the component
22	
23	Place it immediately before the component's `const` declaration:
24	
25	```tsx
26	/** @cf-register */
27	const MyComponent = ({ ... }: MyComponentProps) => { ... };
28	
29	export default MyComponent;
30	```
31	
32	### 3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type
33	
34	Props without a `@cf` tag are silently skipped — omitting the tag is how you exclude a prop from the Contentful definition.
35	
36	```tsx
37	type MyComponentProps = {
38	  /** @cf Headline */
39	  headline: string;
40	
41	  /** @cf Body Copy, longText */
42	  body?: string;
43	
44	  /** @cf Hero Image, media */
45	  heroImage?: string;
46	
47	  /** @cf Layout, select */
48	  layout?: 'left' | 'right';
49	
50	  internalId?: string;
51	};
52	```
53	
54	**Tag syntax:**
55	
56	| Tag | Meaning |
57	|-----|---------|
58	| `/** @cf Display Name */` | Infer control from the TS type (see table below) |
59	| `/** @cf Display Name, control */` | Override the inferred control |
60	
61	Props without any `@cf` tag are silently skipped — no tag needed to exclude a prop.
62	
63	**Type → control inference table:**
64	
65	| TypeScript type | Inferred control | Contentful variable type |
66	|----------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
67	| `string` | `shortText` | Text |
68	| `boolean` | `toggle` | Boolean |
69	| `number` | `number` | Number |
70	| string literal union (`'a' \| 'b'`) | `select` | Text |
71	
72	**Valid explicit controls:** `shortText`, `longText`, `select`, `toggle`, `number`, `media`
73	
74	**Auto-skipped:** props starting with `on` (event handlers), `children` (emits
75	`children: true` on the component registration instead), and any prop with no `@cf` tag.
76	
77	### 4. Run the generator
78	
79	```bash
80	npm run generate:contentful
81	```
82	
83	This rewrites `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`
84	automatically. Verify the output looks correct, then commit both the annotated
85	component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
86	
87	### 5. Verify
88	
89	```bash
90	npx tsc --noEmit
91	npm run generate:contentful:check
92	```
93	
94	`--check` exits zero if `definitions.ts` is in sync with the source files.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Notes
99	
100	- **Never edit `definitions.ts` by hand** — it is autogenerated and will be overwritten
101	  on the next run.
102	- The pre-commit hook auto-runs the generator whenever an `experiences/*.tsx` file is
103	  staged, so `definitions.ts` stays in sync automatically.
104	- `children: ReactNode` → use `children: true` convention; the generator handles this
105	  automatically when it sees a `children` prop.
106	- `thumbnailUrl` is left blank until a real Contentful account exists.
107	- Component `id` is auto-derived as kebab-case of the filename
108	  (`myComponent.tsx` → `my-component`).
109	- Component `name` is auto-derived as Title Case of the id words
110	  (`my-component` → `My Component`).

232	function stripFrontmatter(content) {
233	    const lines = content.split('\n')
234	    if (lines[0].trim() !== '---') {
235	        return content
236	    }
237	    const closingIndex = lines.findIndex((line, i) => i > 0 && line.trim() === '---')
238	    if (closingIndex === -1) {

249	    const lines = content.split('\n')
250	    if (lines[0].trim() !== '---') return null
251	    const closingIndex = lines.findIndex((line, i) => i > 0 && line.trim() === '---')
252	    if (closingIndex === -1) return null
253	    const fmLines = lines.slice(1, closingIndex)
254	    const match = fmLines
255	        .map((line) => line.match(new RegExp(`^${field}:\\s*(.*)$`)))

408	function regenerateTarget(entry) {
409	    const sources = Array.isArray(entry.source) ? entry.source : [entry.source]

412	    const syncedFromComment = `<!-- synced-from: ${syncList} — edit the source(s), not this file, then run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix -->`
413

418	        const frontmatter = buildFrontmatter(entry.frontmatter)

430	            alwaysApply: entry.frontmatter?.alwaysApply ?? false
431	        })
432	        output = `${frontmatter}\n${syncedFromComment}\n\n${body}`
433	    } else if (entry.mode === 'compile') {
434	        const parts = sources.map((s) => {
435	            const body = stripFrontmatter(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, s), 'utf8')).trim()
436	            return `<!-- from: ${s} -->\n\n${body}`
437	        })
438	        const title = entry.title ? `# ${entry.title}\n\n` : ''
439	        output = `${syncedFromComment}\n\n${title}${parts.join('\n\n---\n\n')}\n`
440	    } else {
441	        throw new Error(`Unknown mode '${entry.mode}' for target ${entry.target}`)
442	    }
443	
444	    const targetDir = path.dirname(targetPath)
445	    if (!fs.existsSync(targetDir)) {
446	        fs.mkdirSync(targetDir, {recursive: true})
447	    }
448	    fs.writeFileSync(targetPath, output, 'utf8')
449	}

2	# Pre-commit hook:
3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
8	#
9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
26	
27	  # fnm
28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
30	  fi
31	
32	  # volta
33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
35	  fi
36	
37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
40	    exit 1
41	  fi
42	fi
43	
44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
50	
51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
56	
57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
61	  git add .claude/registry/
62	fi
63	
64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70	
71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
74	    || true)
75	
76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
78	    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
79	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
80	  fi
81	fi
82	
83	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
84	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
85	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
86	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
87	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
88	#     automatically.
89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
90	
91	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
92	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
93	  || true)
94	
95	if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
96	  echo ""
97	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
98	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'
99	
100	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
101	    echo ""
102	    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
103	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
104	  fi
105	
106	  echo ""
107	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
108	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
109	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
110	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
111	  echo ""
112	fi
113	
114	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
115	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
116	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
117	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
118	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
121	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
122	  || true)
123	
124	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
125	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
126	
127	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
128	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
129	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
130	
131	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
132	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
133	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
134	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
135	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
136	    name=$(basename "$f")
137	    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
138	    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
139	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
140	    else
141	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
142	    fi
143	  done
144	
145	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
146	    echo ""
147	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
148	    exit 1
149	  fi
150	
151	  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
152	  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
153	  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
154	fi
155	
156	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
158	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
159	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
160	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
161	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
162	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
163	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	
165	blocked_files=()
166	
167	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
168	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
169	
170	while IFS= read -r file; do
171	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
172	
173	  # Only check files in derived locations
174	  case "$file" in
175	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
176	    *) continue ;;
177	  esac
178	
179	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
180	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
181	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
182	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
183	
184	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
185	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
186	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
187	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
188	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
189	
190	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
191	
192	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
193	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
194	  # Skip it.
195	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
196	  any_source_staged=false
197	  while IFS= read -r src; do
198	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
199	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
200	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
201	      any_source_staged=true
202	      break
203	    fi
204	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
205	  if $any_source_staged; then
206	    continue
207	  fi
208	
209	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
210	  blocked_files+=("$file")
211	
212	done <<< "$modified_staged"
213	
214	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
215	  echo ""
216	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
217	  echo ""
218	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
219	    echo "       $bf"
220	  done
221	  echo ""
222	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
223	  echo ""
224	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
225	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
226	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
227	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
228	  echo ""
229	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
230	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
231	  echo ""
232	  exit 1
233	fi
234	
235	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
237	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
238	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
239	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
240	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
241	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
242	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
243	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
244	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
245	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
246	
247	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
248	  secret_violations=()
249	
250	  while IFS= read -r line; do
251	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
252	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
253	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
254	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
255	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
256	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
257	
258	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
259	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
260	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
261	      continue
262	    fi
263	
264	    # Value looks like a JWT
265	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
266	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
267	      continue
268	    fi
269	
270	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
271	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
272	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
273	      continue
274	    fi
275	
276	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
277	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
278	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
279	      continue
280	    fi
281	
282	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
283	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
284	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
285	      continue
286	    fi
287	
288	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)
289	
290	  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
291	    echo ""
292	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
293	    echo ""
294	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
295	      echo "    $v"
296	    done
297	    echo ""
298	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
299	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
300	    echo ""
301	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
302	    echo ""
303	    exit 1
304	  fi
305	fi
306	
307	exit 0

277	/**
278	 * Extract the component/module-level JSDoc description from file content.
279	 *
280	 * Skips: copyright headers, JSDocs inside line-commented regions, and
281	 * prop-level JSDocs (those followed by an `identifier:` / `identifier?:` line).
282	 * Prefers an explicit `@summary` tag when present.
283	 * Trims to ~200 chars on a sentence boundary.
284	 */
285	function extractDescription(content) {
286	  // Strip whole-line comments so commented-out JSDoc blocks are ignored.
287	  const stripped = content
288	    .split('\n')
289	    .map((l) => (/^\s*\/\//.test(l) ? '' : l))
290	    .join('\n')
291	
292	  const re = /\/\*\*([\s\S]*?)\*\//g
293	  let match
294	  while ((match = re.exec(stripped)) !== null) {
295	    const raw = match[1]
296	    if (raw.includes('Copyright') || raw.includes('SPDX-License')) continue
297	
298	    // The next non-blank line after the JSDoc must be a real top-level
299	    // declaration. This rejects:
300	    //   - prop docs (next line is `name:` or `name?:`)
301	    //   - orphaned JSDocs whose subject is commented out (next line empty
302	    //     after we stripped line comments)
303	    const after = stripped.slice(match.index + match[0].length)
304	    const nextLine = after.split('\n').find((l) => l.trim().length > 0) ?? ''
305	    const isDeclaration =
306	      /^\s*(import\s|(export\s+)?(default\s+)?(async\s+)?(function|const|let|var|class|interface|type|enum)\s)/.test(
307	        nextLine
308	      )
309	    if (!isDeclaration) continue
310	
311	    const lines = raw
312	      .split('\n')
313	      .map((l) => l.replace(/^\s*\*\s?/, '').trim())
314	      .filter((l) => l)
315	
316	    // Prefer @summary if present.
317	    const summaryLine = lines.find((l) => l.startsWith('@summary'))
318	    if (summaryLine) {
319	      const text = summaryLine.replace(/^@summary\s*/, '').trim()
320	      if (text.length > 0) return truncateAtSentence(text, 200)
321	    }
322	
323	    const desc = lines
324	      .filter((l) => !l.startsWith('@'))
325	      .join(' ')
326	      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
327	      .trim()
328	    if (desc.length > 10) return truncateAtSentence(desc, 200)
329	  }
330	  return ''
331	}

333	function truncateAtSentence(text, max) {
334	  if (text.length <= max) return text
335	  const slice = text.slice(0, max)
336	  const lastStop = Math.max(slice.lastIndexOf('. '), slice.lastIndexOf('; '))
337	  if (lastStop > max * 0.5) return slice.slice(0, lastStop + 1)
338	  const lastSpace = slice.lastIndexOf(' ')
339	  return slice.slice(0, lastSpace > 0 ? lastSpace : max) + '…'

361	    const typeWord = m[2]
362	    const rest = m[3] || ''
363	    const required = rest.includes('isRequired')

365	    const typeMap = {
366	      string: 'string',
367	      number: 'number',
368	      bool: 'boolean',

371	      object: 'object',
372	      node: 'node',

1	# Contentful tooling
2	
3	Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.
4	
5	## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)
6	
7	**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `shoppableImage`).
8	**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type.
9	**How:** Push to the Contentful space via the Management API.
10	
11	```bash
12	npm run sync:contentful
13	```
14	
15	Driven by [sync.js](./sync.js). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, and `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` from `.env`. Upserts and publishes each content type.
16	
17	To add a new content type: drop a new file in [content-types/](./content-types/) following the shape of [shoppableImage.js](./content-types/shoppableImage.js), then re-run the sync.
18	
19	## 2. Studio Experiences component definitions (visual builder)
20	
21	**What:** Registers Zimmermann React components with Contentful Studio Experiences so authors can drop them onto pages in the visual builder.
22	**Where:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — one `.tsx` per component, plus a single generated `definitions.ts` registry.
23	**How:** Imported at runtime by `defineComponents` — no push step. The registry is **generated from code**; never edit `definitions.ts` by hand.
24	
25	### Author workflow
26	
27	1. Create or update your component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`.
28	2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration.
29	3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type with a `@cf` JSDoc tag:
30	
31	   ```tsx
32	   type MyComponentProps = {
33	     /** @cf Headline */
34	     headline: string;
35	
36	     /** @cf Hero Image, media */
37	     heroImage?: string;
38	
39	     /** @cf skip */
40	     internalId?: string;
41	   };
42	   ```
43	
44	4. Run the generator:
45	
46	   ```bash
47	   npm run generate:contentful
48	   ```
49	
50	   This rewrites `definitions.ts` automatically. Commit both the annotated component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
51	
52	5. The pre-commit hook runs the generator automatically when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged, keeping `definitions.ts` in sync.
53	
54	For full tag syntax and control options, see the `/contentful-register-component` skill.
55	
56	### CI check
57	
58	```bash
59	npm run generate:contentful:check
60	```
61	
62	Exits zero if `definitions.ts` is up to date, non-zero (with a diff) if regeneration is needed. Wire into CI to catch a forgotten regenerate.
63	
64	## Don't cross the streams
65	
66	- A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does **not** belong in [content-types/](./content-types/) — `sync.js` does not understand it.
67	- A content-type definition (`content-types/*.js`) does **not** belong in `experiences/` — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component.
68	- **Never edit `definitions.ts` directly.** The file is autogenerated; manual edits will be overwritten on the next run.

1	# Git hooks
2	
3	Two hooks ship in this folder:
4	
5	- **`pre-commit`** — regenerates `.claude/registry/`, warns on Contentful definition drift, blocks direct edits to derived AI-config files (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when their `.claude/` source is not also staged, warns when a skill (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) changes without `.claude/skills/README.md` also staged and reminds to update the mirrored Confluence page (no automated push exists yet), and **blocks** any commit where `.env.sample` has a non-empty value for a variable whose name looks like a secret (`TOKEN`/`SECRET`/`KEY`/`PASSWORD`/`CREDENTIAL`) — real values belong only in `.env` (gitignored).

12	If Husky did not install (e.g. cloned with `--no-install` or hooks are not running), install manually:
